  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the root of Netzach is in the innermost aspect of Keter, which is beyond the category of "man" and therefore beyond change or regret.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And the maamar continues in chapter 18</t>
    <t s="2">(the chapter studied this year23</t>
    <t s="3">for the second time,</t>
    <t s="4">"double for wisdom"24),</t>
    <t s="5">that the explanation of the matter</t>
    <t s="6">(that the root of Netzach is in the innerness of Keter)</t>
    <t s="7">will be understood according to what is said25</t>
    <t s="8">"And also the Netzach of Yisrael will not lie and will not regret, for He is not a man to regret,"</t>
    <t s="9">that this—that the Netzach of Yisrael will not regret—is because the root of Netzach is in the aspect of "not a man."</t>
    <t s="10">For the matter of consolation and regret applies only in the aspect of "man."</t>
    <t s="11">And the reason for this is,</t>
    <t s="12">that "man" is intellect and emotions,</t>
    <t s="13">that is, emotions that are based on intellect, and intellect that relates to emotions,</t>
    <t s="14">and therefore change applies to him,</t>
    <t s="15">for since the emotions of man are based on intellect,</t>
    <t s="16">therefore,</t>
    <t s="17">when a change occurs in the intellect, the emotions change.</t>
    <t s="18">And likewise, this is also the case with will that is above intellect,</t>
    <t s="19">that it too is included in the form of man,</t>
    <t s="20">intellect and emotions.</t>
    <t s="21">For in will there are its emotions and its reason,</t>
    <t s="22">a hidden reason.</t>
    <t s="23">And since intellect</t>
    <t s="24">(also the hidden reason)</t>
    <t s="25">is something that changes,</t>
    <t s="26">therefore,</t>
    <t s="27">when a change occurs</t>
    <t s="28">in the hidden reason,</t>
    <t s="29">the will changes</t>
    <t s="30">(the emotions within the will).</t>
    <t s="31">For all this is in the externality of will,</t>
    <t s="32">whose parallel above is the externality of Keter.</t>
    <t s="33">However, in the innerness of Keter,</t>
    <t s="34">where there is no aspect of emotions nor a hidden reason,</t>
    <t s="35">the matter of consolation and regret does not apply there.</t>
    <t s="36">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="37">that this addition in the maamar—that there is no aspect of emotions there—</t>
    <t s="38">[even though the matter of consolation and regret is through the change that occurs in the reason,</t>
    <t s="39">and that in the innerness of will</t>
    <t s="40">(Keter)</t>
    <t s="41">consolation and regret do not apply is,</t>
    <t s="42">seemingly,</t>
    <t s="43">because there is no hidden reason there]</t>
    <t s="44">is,</t>
    <t s="45">because through this the matter of "He is not a man to regret" is better understood.</t>
    <t s="46">For not only is there no cause for the matter of consolation and change in the innerness of Keter</t>
    <t s="47">[for in a will that has a reason,</t>
    <t s="48">since reason is something that changes,</t>
    <t s="49">behold, the change of reason is a cause for the change of will,</t>
    <t s="50">but not so a will that is above reason has no cause to change],</t>
    <t s="51">but moreover,</t>
    <t s="52">it is also not within the category of change at all.</t>
    <t s="53">For in the aspect of the emotions,</t>
    <t s="54">since in the emotions there are two lines,</t>
    <t s="55">Chesed and Gevurah,</t>
    <t s="56">change from Chesed to Gevurah and from Gevurah to Chesed can apply,</t>
    <t s="57">but not so in the innerness of Keter,</t>
    <t s="58">where there is no aspect of emotions,</t>
    <t s="59">that is, it is above the form of lines,</t>
    <t s="60">"there is no left in this Atika"26</t>
    <t s="61">(as brought in the maamar),</t>
    <t s="62">behold, it is not applicable at all that it should change to Gevurah</t>
    <t s="63">(left),</t>
    <t s="64">since there is no left there27,</t>
    <t s="65">and it is entirely right26.</t>
    <t s="66">And this is what is said, "And also the Netzach of Yisrael... will not regret, for He is not a man to regret,"</t>
    <t s="67">that the Netzach of Yisrael is in the aspect of "not a man,"</t>
    <t s="68">the innerness of Keter28.</t>
    <t s="69">And as it is brought in the Zohar29</t>
    <t s="70">on the verse30</t>
    <t s="71">"Behold, He neither slumbers nor sleeps, the Guardian of Yisrael,"</t>
    <t s="72">which is the aspect of one eye</t>
    <t s="73">(above two eyes31),</t>
    <t s="74">the one eye of Atika,</t>
    <t s="75">for in this aspect sleep does not apply,</t>
    <t s="76">"an open eye that does not sleep."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that although Atik is above the form of man, its very name implies it is "removed" from something, thus it has a connection to man, even to the lower man.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, although Atik is above the form of man</t>
    <t s="2">(above lines),</t>
    <t s="3">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="4">from the fact that the matter of Atik</t>
    <t s="5">(above lines)</t>
    <t s="6">comes in the maamar as a continuation of what was explained previously</t>
    <t s="7">(in that same chapter)</t>
    <t s="8">the matter of man</t>
    <t s="9">(that man is intellect and emotions),</t>
    <t s="10">that is,</t>
    <t s="11">that the matter of Atik</t>
    <t s="12">(Atik from the term "removed and separate"32)</t>
    <t s="13">is that it is removed from the form of man,</t>
    <t s="14">it is understood from this that even Atik has a connection to the aspect of man.</t>
    <t s="15">And moreover,</t>
    <t s="16">from the fact that it explains</t>
    <t s="17">(at the beginning of the chapter)</t>
    <t s="18">the matter of man also in the lower man,</t>
    <t s="19">it is understood,</t>
    <t s="20">that the matter of Atik applies also to the lower man,</t>
    <t s="21">for although Atik is the lowest level of Ein Sof,</t>
    <t s="22">as brought in Eitz Chayim33,</t>
    <t s="23">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="24">it applies also to the lower man as above.</t>
    <t s="25">And this matter</t>
    <t s="26">(that Atik applies also to the lower man)</t>
    <t s="27">is not only in the aspect of Atik Yomin,</t>
    <t s="28">but also in Atik</t>
    <t s="29">(unqualified).</t>
    <t s="30">For although Atik</t>
    <t s="31">(unqualified)</t>
    <t s="32">is above Atik Yomin34,</t>
    <t s="33">for the meaning of Atik Yomin is that it is removed from "days,"</t>
    <t s="34">that is, it has a connection to days but is removed from them,</t>
    <t s="35">but not so Atik</t>
    <t s="36">(unqualified)</t>
    <t s="37">is above "days"35,</t>
    <t s="38">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="39">since it is called by the name Atik,</t>
    <t s="40">for the meaning of Atik is "removed,"</t>
    <t s="41">it is necessarily the case,</t>
    <t s="42">that there is a thing from which it is removed.</t>
    <t s="43">And note what is explained in Likkutei Levi Yitzchak36</t>
    <t s="44">regarding a discussion about these levels of Atik Yomin and Atika d'Atikin etc.,</t>
    <t s="45">that the discussion there relates to what is explained above.</t>
    <t s="46">See there.</t>
    <t s="47">And from the fact that the maamar explains the matter of man also in the lower man,</t>
    <t s="48">it is understood,</t>
    <t s="49">that the matter from which Atik is removed,</t>
    <t s="50">that is, that it has some connection to it,</t>
    <t s="51">is also in the lower man.</t>
    <t s="52">And moreover,</t>
    <t s="53">that this matter</t>
    <t s="54">(that Atik applies also to the lower man)</t>
    <t s="55">is in all the levels of Atik,</t>
    <t s="56">even in the innerness of Atik,</t>
    <t s="57">for although regarding the innerness of Atik the Tzemach Tzedek explains that it is the aspect of Ein Sof itself37,</t>
    <t s="58">and "until it is called His very Essence"38,</t>
    <t s="59">nevertheless, since it is called by the name Atik, meaning removed,</t>
    <t s="60">it is necessarily the case that there is a thing from which it is removed,</t>
    <t s="61">which includes</t>
    <t s="62">(as above)</t>
    <t s="63">also the lower man.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section demonstrates from various sources that the concept of Atik, being above lines and change, is relevant to the lower man, even in his lowest state, and is analogous to the natural state of a "elder."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">And so it is also understood from what the Mitteler Rebbe says in Toras Chayim39</t>
    <t s="2">in explaining the matter of Atik being above lines</t>
    <t s="3">(one eye above the division into Chesed and Gevurah),</t>
    <t s="4">that he first introduces40</t>
    <t s="5">the matter of the division into Chesed and Gevurah that comes from the intellect</t>
    <t s="6">(the lines of Chesed and Gevurah in the aspect of man),</t>
    <t s="7">and that from the perspective of the intellect, it is possible that the same reasoning will change and be reversed</t>
    <t s="8">(and several times)</t>
    <t s="9">from merit to liability and from liability to merit</t>
    <t s="10">(the matter of consolation and change in the aspect of man),</t>
    <t s="11">and that this matter in the aspect of man</t>
    <t s="12">(the matter of the division into Chesed and Gevurah and the matter of consolation and change)</t>
    <t s="13">is also in the lower man,</t>
    <t s="14">and moreover,</t>
    <t s="15">that all this is explained there on the verse41</t>
    <t s="16">"And Hashem said... I will go down now and see if according to its outcry"</t>
    <t s="17">(of Sodom),</t>
    <t s="18">the descent of the Supernal Man to see the outcry of Sodom</t>
    <t s="19">[from which it is understood,</t>
    <t s="20">that the analogy for this from the lower man is also as he is found in the most degraded state],</t>
    <t s="21">and after this introduction comes the explanation of the matter of Atik,</t>
    <t s="22">that is, that the matter of Atik is that it is removed from this aspect of man that was explained previously,</t>
    <t s="23">from which it is understood,</t>
    <t s="24">that the matter of Atik applies also to the lower man,</t>
    <t s="25">even as he is in the most degraded state.</t>
    <t s="26">And so it is also understood from what the Rebbe Maharash explains in the maamar "Mayim Rabim"42</t>
    <t s="27">regarding the change that occurred through "And He smelled the pleasing aroma" after the flood43,</t>
    <t s="28">and the matter of Atik is that it is removed from this.</t>
    <t s="29">And there is another matter in this,</t>
    <t s="30">that in "Mayim Rabim" there,</t>
    <t s="31">in the continuation of the matter of Atik,</t>
    <t s="32">it is explained</t>
    <t s="33">(not only regarding the matter of the "thorn" of the Yud,</t>
    <t s="34">and not even only regarding the matter of the Yud,</t>
    <t s="35">but also)</t>
    <t s="36">regarding the matter of the Hei of the Name Havayah.</t>
    <t s="37">And so it is understood from what the Rebbe</t>
    <t s="38">(the Rebbe Rashab)</t>
    <t s="39">of blessed memory says in the maamar "Heichaltzu" 567244</t>
    <t s="40">that Atik means "elder"45</t>
    <t s="41">because the aspect of Atik</t>
    <t s="42">(in which there are no changes)</t>
    <t s="43">is analogous to an elder in its simple sense</t>
    <t s="44">[for just as an elder is not affected</t>
    <t s="45">(and changed)</t>
    <t s="46">by something contrary to his will,</t>
    <t s="47">so too is it with Atik,</t>
    <t s="48">that affect and change do not apply to it],</t>
    <t s="49">from this comparison of Atik to an elder in its simple sense</t>
    <t s="50">(which is in the lower man),</t>
    <t s="51">it is understood that this is a natural matter that Atik applies in the lower man.</t>
    <t s="52">And moreover,</t>
    <t s="53">that this—that Atik applies to the lower man—is also for a youth</t>
    <t s="54">(and even before that),</t>
    <t s="55">since then it is in his potential to be an elder</t>
    <t s="56">[and to the extent that through the manner of conduct in his youth,</t>
    <t s="57">so will be</t>
    <t s="58">(consequently)</t>
    <t s="59">also the conduct in his old age,</t>
    <t s="60">as it is said46</t>
    <t s="61">"Train a youth according to his way, even when he grows old he will not depart from it"],</t>
    <t s="62">and it is only lacking time.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
